title: Entryflow zones and compact shell — IA + routing walkthrough (WIP)
content:
Context / goal:
- Problem: current console nav mixes contextual entry points (jobs, models, billing, routes) with global admin utilities; users lose task focus when switching between "surfaces".
- Goal: introduce a "zone-first" mental model + compact shell to reduce cognitive load and make deep-linking predictable. Keep routes shallow and stable for third-party integrations.

High-level proposal summary (short):
- Top-level 'Entryflow Zones' (left edge of shell): Work, Billing, Admin, Integrations, Support. Each zone is a curated surface (a set of pages + primary actions) rather than a flat nav item.
- Compact shell collapses less-used chrome: breadcrumbs + quick actions remain visible on collapse; zone switcher is persistent as slim glyph + tooltip.
- Routing contract: canonical route = /zone/:zoneId/[primaryPage]/:resourceId? with optional query flags for panel state.

Rationale / design principles:
- Task-first: surfaces should map to user goals (ship model, monitor traffic, tune cost).
- Predictable deep links: external systems (CI, tickets) should be able to link to a stable canonical route.
- Progressive disclosure: start compact, expand into sub-navigation only when user drills in.
- Keyboard-first access and screenreader semantics preserved.

Wireframe writeup (verbal):
- Shell components:
  - Zone rail (leftmost): icons + 24px touch target. Hover reveals zone label and recent 3 actions. Click selects zone and navigates to zone home.
  - Compact header (top): breadcrumb slot, page title, quick actions (Run, Stop, New).
  - Secondary rail (contextual): only visible when zone is active and show >1 primary pages; otherwise hidden.

Zone home behaviour:
- /zone/work -> consolidated workspace: recent projects, active endpoints, recommended prompts.
- /zone/dedicated -> capacity overview (summary cards) and per-pool quick-actions.
- /zone/observe -> graphs and traces; default metric filters preserved in URL.

Routing semantics and examples:
- Canonical routes: /zone/work/projects/alpha-tokenizer.
- Panel overlays are NOT separate routes unless they are linkable (shareable evals, run detail). For ephemeral modals keep query param like ?modal=share to avoid route explosion.
- Back/forward UX: toggling rail collapse should NOT pollute history. Panel open should push state (so shareable).

Accessibility and keyboard flows (notes):
- Zone rail: tabbable list, aria-current when selected.
- Compact collapse toggle: visible label in sr-only.
- Quick action modal: focus trap, restore focus to invoking action.

Backlog grooming snippets (tickets to create / refine):
- CONSOLE-987 (linked) - Zone model + API contract: implement /zone/:zoneId canonical resolver (owner: Priya). Acceptance: route resolves to zone home, breadcrumbs populate, telemetry fired.
- CONSOLE-1021 - Compact shell visual tokens + theme variables (owner: Ethan). Acceptance: collapsed state matches Figma tokens, icons adapt to dark mode.
- CONSOLE-1043 - Keyboard flow QA (owner: Liam). Acceptance: full nav usable with keyboard alone, SR announcements verified.
- CONSOLE-1106 - Deep-link regression tests for legacy routes (owner: eng-platform).

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to discuss):
- How many zones? Minimal set vs. flexible org-configurable zones. (Perf vs. customizability).
- Do we allow per-team pins inside zone rail? If yes, need feature flag for GA.
- Side-effect of compact shell: will saved bookmarks break for users used to full left-rail deep links? Need migration shim.

Telemetry and observability hooks (quick):
- Events: zone_select, zone_home_view, secondary_rail_open, compact_toggle.
- Attributes: user_tier, org_size_bucket, route_path, session_id.
- Goal: correlate zone_select -> 7-day retention and feature adoption.

Rollout plan / safety:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5% orgs behind 'zone-shell' feature flag, route aliasing enabled, collect metrics for errors + bounce.
- Phase 2 (opt-in beta): make opt-in in account settings + CTA in onboarding.
- Phase 3 (GA): enable by default with migration banner + legacy route redirects.

Migration notes for internal infra:
- Router layer: add a resolver that maps legacy top-level paths to /zone/:zoneId/ equivalent. Keep a mapping table in router-config repo.
- Server side rendering: ensure zone home preloads critical cards for faster TTI.

Mock microcopy and inline labels (examples):
- Zone tooltip (compact): "Work — projects, endpoints, quick-run"
- Collapsed quick-action label: "+ New" (creates resource in current zone).
- Breadcrumb placeholder: "Home > Work > Projects > alpha-tokenizer"

Edge cases observed in user testing notes (raw):
- Users with lots of routes expect full hierarchy visible — compact shell hides discoverability. Need a 'reveal' affordance.
- Support agents need a quick-launch to switch org context; add a command-palette hook (global) rather than burying in zones.

Quick wireframe todo (engineering + design):
- [ ] Prototype slim rail animation (Priya) - ticket CONSOLE-1032
- [ ] Route resolver + legacy mapping (Eng infra) - CONSOLE-987 subtask
- [ ] Integrations panel design for 'Integrations' zone (Ethan)
- [ ] Accessibility runbook + checklist (Liam)

Acceptance criteria (minimum for MVP):
- Zone rail selectable, persists state across reloads, compact toggle works without history pollution.
- Canonical routes resolve and backlinks/shortlinks continue to work.
- No regressions in LR metrics (latency, TTI) beyond 10% for canary orgs.

Miscellaneous notes / quick brain dump:
- Consider making Zone icons semantically colored (status badges) when there are alerts in that surface.
- Command palette should respect zone context and offer 'Open zone home' action.
- Investigate server-side caching for zone home cards (ttl 30s) to keep view snappy.

Questions for review meeting (next Wed):
1) Do we lock zones into product-defined set or allow org-defined pins?
2) Is breadcrumb enough for discoverability or do we need persistent labels on collapsed rail?
3) What telemetry threshold decides rollback for canary?

References + links:
- CONSOLE-987 (proto + router mapping)
- Figma: Compact Shell v2 (internal link in Confluence)
- Slack thread: #console-navigation (design thread 2026-02-20)

Notes to self: keep copy short in tooltips, minimize cognitive overhead for first-time users. Follow up with UX research to test 3-zone vs. 5-zone layouts (qual + quant).
